ratings_why.fun: Good tier shape from Button Mushroom to Puffwell and Bootlace, but income comes from dying, so a winning board earns less and the late game can stall.
ratings_why.distinct: Fruits paying fixed lumps in reading order is a placement-and-change puzzle no current tribe has, though the counter itself echoes the Larder and Toll.

verdict_why: Amanita's wording needs one real fix; the rest is ideas, and the core works.

points.text: Warden Amanita: "share its stats" can mean each neighbour gets all of them or they split them. Say which, e.g. "split its stats between them".

Compost slows down as your board gets stronger and loses fewer units. A small trickle that doesn't need deaths (say 1 Compost per enemy your board kills) would keep the top end growing after you start winning.
Losing rounds 1-3 costs no Health but banks Compost. Counting deaths in those rounds at half, as the designer suggests, keeps the throw-early line from being the default.
Clerk Inkcap's Health clock is great flavour; with Bootlace he loses 2 a turn. Saying whether the free trigger also costs Health would help.
Foxfire Lantern-bearer only reaches the one or two units diagonally in front of it. Making it units touching this would tie it to the network idea and give it a better placement puzzle.

standouts.why: Bellows Puffwell, repeated while you can pay, makes Fruit order a real decision every turn, and it's a big permanent payoff.
Grandmother Bootlace is a clear capstone the whole spend build points at, the Brann of Fruits.
Old Fingers turns a dead slot or a spare Created unit into 4 Compost, a fresh way to buy power at Tier 3.

weakest.why: Ludwig grows at most +2/+2 a fight and asks for a board shape before you have one.
Foxfire Lantern-bearer reaches few units and fights Fruits for the same pile.
Hired Mute's Compost-for-gold trade is clever, but at Tier 2 you usually need the gold more.

flags.note: Puffwell with Three-Rain Mourner and Bootlace gives about +8/+8 to every unit a turn, more with goldens. Dying less as you grow slows it, but it's the first card to watch.
With Three-Rain Mourner, each Sexton Spore gives back the 2 it cost, so five 4/4s a fight cost nothing. The five-a-fight cap stops it running away.
"Share its stats" is ambiguous: split between the neighbours, or each gets the full amount.
